note.question: How do no permanent friend and enemy compare for impacts of the IIoT-based platform in the maintenance service market?
note.overview: As the industrial Internet-of-things (IIoT) is becoming increasingly valuable, manufacturers are eager to establish IIoT-based platforms for preventative maintenance (PM). These platforms reposition the roles of manufacturers and reshape the patterns of the after-sales service market. Manufacturers can adopt either the competitive strategy by introducing improved after-sales services to compete with independent maintenance, repair, and operations firms (MROs) or the “coopetitive” strategy by simultaneously opening the platform to these MROs.

source.quote: These platforms reposition the roles of manufacturers and reshape the patterns of the after-sales service market.
These platforms reposition the roles of manufacturers and reshape the patterns of the after-sales service market.

Manufacturers can adopt either the competitive strategy by introducing improved after-sales services to compete with independent maintenance, repair, and operations firms (MROs) or the “coopetitive” strategy by simultaneously opening the platform to these MROs.

Because this decision remains unaddressed in the past literature, the first key question we investigate is as follows: Should the manufacturer establish an IIoT-based platform for PM when the product value for customers is rel­ atively high and the IIoT adoption reduces product failures?
Our study provides an important implication for managers that the opening of the platform can increase the total revenue and compensate for the negative impact of ser­ vice competition.
An independent MRO (denoted with subscript R) is also considered to provide after-sales service for prod­ uct owners at a price pR.
Under NP scheme, both the manufacturer and MRO offer the improved after-sales services and determine their PM effort levels (i.e., uM and uR).
